answer: No TUI until a compelling case appears. Surfaces: (1) a CLI chooser — transient, fuzzy, one keystroke, Enter attaches; (2) a small Emacs plugin calling the core; (3) composition rather than features — umbriel IPC for windows, notify-send for attention. Splits, tabs and layout are ghostty's and umbriel's job, and building either would work against the grain.
body: Three shapes: (1) an attached TUI — persistent sidebar, spaces/tabs, preview pane, keys to attach/kill/label, needing layout and focus decisions; (2) a summon-picker — one keystroke from the WM or shell, fuzzy list annotated like the elisp's completing-read, Enter attaches and exits; (3) a read-only status line or notification feed on top of (2). Most of zmux's cost sits here.
title: What is the human surface?
